summary: The denial prevention workflows have a measured result in finance's own reporting, but the executive sponsor left six weeks ago and no business owner is named for a contract the interim CFO is reviewing. Front-end adoption is falling and the new stakeholder feels the tool was bought without her.

indicators.evidence: The sponsor left; the VP role is unfilled; the interim CFO has no relationship with the vendor.
indicators.quote: Since Linda left, the interim CFO's office is reviewing every contract that renews in the next two quarters.

indicators.evidence: The operational champion speaks strongly to value; the business stakeholder does not.
indicators.quote: Which is crazy, because this is the one tool I'd fight for.

indicators.evidence: A manager-level champion and a Director who is not yet bought in. No executive.
indicators.quote: But I'm a manager, I can't just book the CFO.

indicators.evidence: Sponsor departed; contract owner field is blank; the Director has not agreed to take ownership.
indicators.quote: Linda was the owner. Now it's, I guess, a blank.

indicators.evidence: Denial prevention is the clear objective, but no formal target was mentioned.
indicators.quote: when we launched the denial prevention workflows, our initial denial rate was eleven point eight percent

indicators.evidence: Denial rate baseline of 11.8% from monthly revenue cycle reports that finance receives.
indicators.quote: That's from the revenue cycle reports, the ones finance gets every month.

indicators.evidence: Denial rate measured at 8.9% last month and under 9% for three months, in finance's own report.
indicators.quote: Last month it was eight point nine. It's been under nine for three months now.

indicators.evidence: The champion owns the story; the business stakeholder and executives do not.
indicators.quote: And someone telling me what my team gets out of it. Not what revenue cycle gets.

indicators.evidence: Back-office revenue cycle use is steady; patient access logins are down about a third since summer.
indicators.quote: Patient access logins are down about a third since the summer.

indicators.evidence: Denial prevention workflows are embedded in revenue cycle operations.
indicators.quote: The back-office revenue cycle side is steady.

indicators.evidence: New front-end staff were never trained, and the workflows depend on how they enter data.
indicators.quote: with turnover, a lot of my new staff were never trained on it

indicators.evidence: The QBR was cancelled twice; no full review since spring.
indicators.quote: our QBR got cancelled twice this year, so we haven't had a full review since spring

indicators.evidence: The champion is proactive; the Director attended mainly because of procurement.
indicators.quote: I'm here partly because Nate asked me to be, and partly because I got an email from procurement

indicators.evidence: The denial rate is finance's own number, but the dollar estimate is unvalidated and no executive has acknowledged it.
indicators.quote: Finance hasn't looked at my math, but the denial rate itself is their number.

maturity.rationale: A measured outcome exists in finance's own reporting, but leadership recognition was lost with the sponsor's departure and front-end adoption is slipping. Holding this stage depends on a named owner and an executive who has seen the result.

keyPlayers.name: Linda (surname not given)
keyPlayers.title: Former VP, Revenue Cycle
keyPlayers.note: Left about six weeks ago; was the contract owner.

keyPlayers.name: Nate Alvarez
keyPlayers.title: Revenue Cycle Manager
keyPlayers.note: Built the program with Linda; cannot reach the CFO directly.

keyPlayers.name: Monica Hale
keyPlayers.title: Director, Patient Access
keyPlayers.note: Open to ownership if the training issue is fixed; checking with her manager.

keyPlayers.name: Greg (surname not given)
keyPlayers.title: Interim CFO
keyPlayers.note: In cost-cutting mode; responds to money, not features.

kpis.name: Claim value not denied (annualized)
kpis.source: Champion's calculation; not validated by finance
kpis.note: Label as an estimate in all materials.

useCases.name: Front-end registration and eligibility steps
useCases.evidence: Live, but patient access usage is down about a third.

risks.text: No named business owner, with procurement requiring one by mid-November.
Interim CFO is in cut-what-you-can mode and has no relationship with the vendor.
Renewal in January, about three months away.
Untrained front-end staff could erode the denial result over time.

opportunities.text: Finance already owns the denial rate number, so the core result is credible.
Registration error reduction could be a win for the patient access team.
The Director can likely get 15 minutes with the interim CFO.

actions.action: Get 15 minutes with the interim CFO
actions.detail: Champion asks the Director to request the slot; lead with finance's own denial rate trend and present the dollar figure clearly as an estimate pending validation.
Support the Director's conversation with her manager. Remove the training objection first so she can say yes.

actions.action: Fix front-end training without pulling staff off the phones
actions.detail: Turn on in-workflow guides for patient access and deliver a short training plan this week.

actions.action: Validate the dollar estimate with finance
actions.detail: Walk finance through the champion's method so the $1.1M can be stated as validated or replaced.
Offer a vendor executive for the CFO conversation to signal accountability, not to sell.
Book a short monthly review with the Director and champion through renewal.

statedFacts: Denial rate fell from 11.8% at launch to 8.9% last month, and has been under 9% for three months (finance's revenue cycle reports).
The champion estimates about $1.1M per year in claims not denied; finance has not validated this.
valueNarrative.draft: Since launch, Sagebrook's denial rate has fallen from 11.8% to 8.9% and has held under 9% for three months. That figure comes from the revenue cycle reports finance already receives. Our working estimate of the dollar impact is about $1.1M a year, which we will validate with finance before relying on it.
caveats: The $1.1M figure is an unvalidated estimate.

projection.text: If nothing changes, the contract goes into a cost-cutting review with no owner and no executive who has seen the result, and a measurable win is at real risk of non-renewal in January.

missingInformation.question: Who will be the named business owner, and when?
Did front-end registration errors fall after launch?
missingInformation.why: Would give the patient access team its own reason to support renewal.

missingInformation.question: Does finance accept the method behind the $1.1M estimate?
What target denial rate does Sagebrook want?
Is there any interest in additional use cases?

assumptions: The dollar objective is inferred from the champion's estimate, not a stated business objective.
